evals.prompt: I want to build a first-person shooter. Help me set up the whole gameplay data — I'm not sure exactly what I need yet.
evals.expected_output: Should run GUIDED mode: discover the genre packs under genres/, present a menu, and recognize this maps to the shooter pack. Should read genres/shooter/spec.adoc and load genres/shooter/entities/, then ask a tight round of brief questions (player/enemies, which abilities to keep, resources and starting values, win/lose). Then scaffold the four pillars (Attributes+Set, tag registry, Abilities, Effects) plus a Gameplay Controller for the player into schemas/examples/<game>/, delegating per-entity YAML to ugas-schema-author. Every file carries the %%UGAS_VERSION%% $schema placeholder. Finishes by running python scripts/validate_schema_examples.py, fixing errors, and summarizing the player loop and the ExecCalc_* engine seams (ExecCalc_MagazineReload, ExecCalc_HitResolution) to implement.

assertions.text: All produced entities are schema-valid (validate_dir.py reports all_valid with zero failures).
Defines all four pillars plus a Gameplay Controller: an attribute set, a tag registry, at least one ability, at least one effect, and at least one gameplay_controller.
Anchored on the matching shooter pack: reuses the pack's tag vocabulary and entity structure rather than inventing a from-scratch taxonomy.

All cross-references resolve — ability Cost/Cooldown point at real effects, modifier attributes exist in the attribute set, and every referenced tag is declared in the registry or owned by the core registry.
Preserves the FPS signature mechanic: ballistic hit-resolution, aim-down-sights, and magazine reload.
Names ExecCalc_* engine seams for non-declarative math instead of faking it in data (e.g. ExecCalc_HitResolution / ExecCalc_MagazineReload).
Stays additive to the core spec — does NOT redeclare the core lifecycle tags (State.Alive / State.Combat / State.Dead) that the core registry already owns.

evals.prompt: build a kart racer: 4 players, drift-to-boost, item pickups, first to 3 laps wins. Give me the whole thing in one go, no questions.
evals.expected_output: Should run ONE-SHOT mode: fuzzy-match 'kart racer' to the racing pack (the nearest available pack), load genres/racing/entities/ as the base, and scaffold a complete schema-valid game definition without interactive Q&A — four pillars plus a Gameplay Controller — inferring sensible defaults for anything the brief omits. Should extend additively (drift-to-boost and item pickups as new Effects + Abilities + State.* tags granted by Effects, reusing the racing pack's traction calc). Writes to schemas/examples/<game>/ with %%UGAS_VERSION%% $schema on every file, validates with scripts/validate_schema_examples.py, and returns a short note of the assumptions made and the ExecCalc_* seams to implement. The lap-count win condition should map to real state/attributes.

assertions.text: All produced entities are schema-valid (validate_dir.py reports all_valid with zero failures).
Defines all four pillars plus a Gameplay Controller: an attribute set, a tag registry, at least one ability, at least one effect, and at least one gameplay_controller.
Anchored on the matching racing pack: reuses the pack's Vehicle.* / Surface.* vocabulary and entity structure rather than inventing a from-scratch taxonomy.

All cross-references resolve — ability Cost/Cooldown point at real effects, modifier attributes exist in the attribute set, and every referenced tag is declared in the registry or owned by the core registry.
Preserves the kart signature mechanic: drift-to-boost (charge then release) built on the racing pack's traction model, reusing ExecCalc_VehicleTraction rather than reinventing the grip pipeline.
Names ExecCalc_* engine seams for non-declarative math instead of faking it in data (e.g. ExecCalc_VehicleTraction, lap/standings resolution).
Stays additive to the core spec — does NOT redeclare the core lifecycle tags (State.Alive / State.Combat / State.Dead) that the core registry already owns.

evals.prompt: Just write me a single poison damage-over-time effect that does 8 damage per second for 10 seconds.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is a SINGLE-ENTITY request, not whole-game scaffolding, and defer to the ugas-schema-author skill rather than running the genre-first whole-game workflow. Should not discover genre packs or scaffold four pillars for a lone effect.

assertions.text: Produces exactly one GameplayEffect and no whole-game scaffold (no attribute set, tag registry, abilities, or controller).
Encodes the poison DOT correctly: DurationPolicy HasDuration, Period 1.0s, Duration 10.0s, and a single Add modifier of -8 to Health.
Routes the request to the ugas-schema-author skill rather than running the genre-first whole-game workflow.
